hooks: You can describe data with a mean and a spread. How likely is an event, and how does new evidence change it?
Probability rules are set. How can a small sample tell you about a whole population?
Samples vary. How do you say how far off your estimate might be?
An interval gives a range. How do you decide whether a difference is real or just noise?
Tests can be wrong in two ways. How do you design an A/B test that avoids the common traps?
The test shows a lift. Does that prove the change caused it?
Correlation is not cause. How do you read a line fitted through data, and its coefficients?
Linear regression predicts a number. What changes when the answer is yes or no?
statistics.upNext: Next: ML fundamentals. Use these ideas to train models, split data honestly and measure how well they work.

hooks: You know the kinds of learning. How do you split data so your score is honest?
The split is safe. What do you do to raw columns before a model sees them?
Features are ready. Which models handle tabular data well: trees, forests, boosting?
A deep tree memorizes the training data. How do bias, variance and regularization explain that?
You can tune the fit. Which number tells you whether the model is actually good?
Accuracy can look great and still be useless. What if one class is rare?
Tabular models are covered. How do neural networks learn their own features?
ml-fundamentals.upNext: Next: the code behind the models. Python data tools, pandas and NumPy, for cleaning and shaping data.

hooks: Arrays are fast and uniform. How does pandas add labels and mixed types on top?
You can select rows and columns. What do you do with the gaps, the NaN values?
The data is clean enough. How do you split it by key and summarize each group?
One table is summarized. What goes wrong when you join two tables on a key?
The code is correct but slow. Why is apply a trap, and where do dtypes and Polars help?
Fast and right. How do you plot it and keep the notebook tidy enough to trust?
python-data.upNext: Next: a model in a notebook is a draft. MLOps covers tracking, deploying and monitoring it in production.

hooks: The lifecycle has many steps. How do you record every experiment so none is lost?
Runs are logged. Can anyone rerun one and get the same result?
Pipelines are reproducible. How do you version models, data and code together?
Versions are tracked. How do training and serving use the same features without drift?
Features are shared. How do you test and release a model like any other software?
The model ships. Should it answer in batch, or online within milliseconds?
It is serving. How do you try a new model on real traffic without risking users?
A new model is live. How do you notice when the data or accuracy slowly drifts?
ml-ops.upNext: Next: models that generate text. LLM applications cover tokens, retrieval, agents and evaluation.

hooks: The model reads tokens in a limited context. How do you ask it so the answer has a reliable shape?
Prompts only know what you tell them. How do you find the right text among thousands of documents?
Vectors find similar text. How do you cut documents into chunks and rerank what comes back?
Good chunks and ranking exist. How do you put them together so answers come from your data?
RAG answers questions. How does a model call tools and act, not just talk?
The app can act. How do you measure whether its answers are right and not made up?
You can score quality. What stops a malicious prompt or leaked personal data?
It is safe enough. Why are the bill and latency high, and how do you cut both?
